setup: Euler's theorem: a function homogeneous of degree \(k\) satisfies \(x f_x + y f_y = k f(x, y)\).

steps.say: Every term of \([[ftex]]\) has total degree [[degree]], so \(f(tx, ty) = t^{[[degree]]} f(x, y)\): the degree is [[degree]].
Euler's theorem then gives \(x f_x + y f_y = [[degree]] \cdot [[f]] = [[value]]\), with no partial derivative to compute.
